newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Mobutu entitled to medical care.
newsitem.headline: France says Mobutu entitled to medical care.

text.p: France indicated on Wednesday that it may be prepared to freeze the assets of ousted Zaire president Mobutu Sese Seko but may admit him for medical treatment.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe, asked in a television interview if the government would freeze Mobutu's assets, as Switzerland has, said: "We will apply legal rules, in as much as we will be asked to."

Mobutu owns a mansion on the Riviera and an apartment in Paris' most expensive avenue Foch. Supporters of the government of the newly renamed Democratic Republic of Congo say his family also owns property in France.
Juppe said he had not received any request to give Mobutu political asylum.
Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain hinted earlier that France might be prepared to admit him for medical treatment.

"There has been no request made to France. As none has been made, we will not make a decision on something which does not exist. But we hope he can get the treatment that any sick person deserves," he said.

Mobutu, who is currently in the Togo capital of Lome, has received regular treatment for prostate cancer at a hospital in Monaco in recent months while recuperating from surgery at his palatial villa near the Riviera resort of Nice.
An embarrassed France has been reluctant to say whether it would admit its former ally following his ouster by rebel leader Laurent Kabila, who has proclaimed himself president.
There has been widespread speculation in France that Mobutu would end go to his Riviera estate, but only after a French parliamentary election which ends on June 1.
